source_review.reason: The corrected guest predicate cannot pass on the Suspense shell alone: it requires the selected, linked active Chat pane plus both ChatView-owned markers, no Suspense fallback, the guest avatar, and complete Screenshots absence. These markers are real normal ChatHeader children rather than strings in a popover, title attribute, or the fallback: ChatView renders the guest guidance as a plain span and New chat as a real Button in its header; the fallback is only a spinning Loader2. After reload and after local sign-out from admin-selected Screenshots, the same predicate is awaited. The runner only observes Chat after those transitions and never clicks New chat or submits a chat turn.
evidence: guestNavigation scopes all pane and Chat markers to the unique active top-level tabpanel and requires it to be linked to the uniquely selected target tab with positive height.

ChatView.tsx renders `Sign in to choose an agent` as a normal header span for signed-out users and renders `New chat` as an actual Button in the same ChatHeader; repository search finds the exact markers only at those source locations.

App.tsx wraps the lazy ChatView in Suspense with TabFallback, which contains only a Loader2 spinner. The required ChatView markers therefore distinguish its mounted component from the fallback even if the fallback is otherwise present in the active pane.
guestViewAccepted requires chatComponentMounted and guestChatGuidancePresent for Chat, and independently rejects the fallback, admin avatar, Screenshots trigger/pane/content, or any non-guest state.

Both the real guest reload branch and real admin Screenshots-to-local-signout branch call selectedGuestView('Chat'); that helper waits on the full predicate. The runner does not click the New chat button, compose, or send a chat message.
